# clipvolume

> A macOS menu bar volume control with a per-app mixer. It shows every app currently producing audio with a live level meter, gives each app its own volume slider and mute button, and can play/pause Spotify, Music, TV, QuickTime Player and VLC directly. No virtual audio driver, no kernel extension, no Accessibility permission. Free for personal use.

clipvolume replaces the Sound icon in the macOS menu bar. Clicking it shows a master volume slider, a mute button and an output-device picker. A "Mixer ›" row expands to list every app that is producing audio, each with a live level meter, a per-app slider (relative to master), a mute button, and — for supported media apps — a play/pause button. Per-app settings last until that app relaunches. Media apps playing somewhere other than the Mac (for example Spotify via Spotify Connect) still get a row with a working pause button.

Key facts:
- Platform: macOS 14.4 (Sonoma) or later. Apple silicon and Intel.
- Price: free for personal use, licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0. Commercial use requires permission. Source code on GitHub.
- Distribution: direct download (.dmg) from GitHub Releases, signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Not on the Mac App Store because Core Audio process taps do not work reliably in the App Store sandbox.
- Technology: Core Audio process taps (macOS 14.2+ API). No virtual audio device, no kernel extension.
- Permissions: none for master volume, device picker, or the list of apps making sound. "System Audio Recording" (one prompt) for the per-app mixer. "Automation" (one prompt per app) for play/pause. Never asks for Accessibility.
- Privacy: no network connections, nothing recorded or saved to disk.
- Author/publisher: Michael Moore.
- Current version: 0.1.0.

## Common questions
- Which app is making that noise? Open the Mixer; the app whose meter is moving is the one playing.
- Can it pause a YouTube tab? No — browsers don't expose play/pause — but it can mute the tab's app instantly.
- Does it need Accessibility? No.
- Related apps by the same author: clipandcue (clipboard history, clipandcue.com) and clipandnote (screenshot markup, clipandnote.com).
